sections.label: Case Study
sections.h2: Thirteen AI assistants at a private dining club in Vail
body: For a private dining club in Vail, Colorado, we built 13 AI assistants into the club's own software. The concierge assistant answers "can we seat 2 at 7?" from real availability. The host assistant greets parties, looks up guests, proposes tables, and works by voice. The server brief writes a greeting when the party sits.

Behind the scenes, a scheduling assistant drafts weeks and covers call-outs, a read-only analyst studies kitchen pacing, and an "ask the club" assistant answers read-only questions across all the data and drafts emails a person sends. Every one of them has a person confirming anything that books, publishes, or sends.
Read the full case study. The assistants live inside our custom restaurant software, and the menu import feeds our staff training academies.

faq.q: How much does AI for a restaurant cost?
faq.a: The assessment is free. Beyond that, every engagement is scoped to your restaurant, so there's no price list. You'll get a written plan with priorities, budget, and timeline, and nothing starts until you approve it.

faq.q: How long does it take to set up an AI assistant?
faq.a: It depends on the assistant and the information it needs. Your plan lays out the timeline, and you review each assistant with real examples before your team relies on it.

faq.q: Does it work with my POS?
faq.a: Our assistants work alongside your POS. They read the systems we build for you, like reservations, guest files, schedules, and menus, plus the documents you share. Your POS keeps handling orders and payments the way it does today.

faq.q: Will the AI ever book a table or post something on its own?
faq.a: No. A person confirms anything that books, publishes, or sends. Assistants answer questions, draft, and suggest, and someone on your team approves the action.

faq.q: What do I need to provide?
faq.a: Access to what each assistant should work from, such as menu files, your handbook, house rules, and brand voice, plus a manager to review drafts while we tune it. We do the work. You guide the process.

faq.q: Does this work for one restaurant or a group?
faq.a: Both. A single restaurant might start with review replies and server briefs. A group can roll the same assistants out to every location, with one standard for how teams use them.
